caption: Before: hyp.load('sotus') returned the wrong hosted dataset (a NIPS topic model), so the State of the Union example rendered a degenerate triangle with stray topic-word labels instead of speeches.
After: load('sotus') restored to the real 29 State of the Union addresses (1989-2018); the example now traces a genuine text trajectory through semantic space via the default text pipeline.
Before (critical): smoothing a list of datasets ran across the dataset boundary, so subject A (all 0) and subject B (all 1) silently contaminated each other at the seam.
After (regenerated on the fixed branch, same scenario): Smooth is applied per dataset, so A stays exactly 0 and B stays exactly 1 with no cross-subject bleed at the boundary.
Before: static line plots silently dropped the trajectory's final samples, so a huge 50-sigma spike at the end of a 901-point series is completely invisible (flat line).
After: the full series is drawn to its final sample and the terminal 50-sigma spike is clearly visible.
Before: the color letter in a marker+line combo fmt was silently dropped, so fmt='ro-' rendered in the default palette's salmon instead of red.
After: fmt='ro-' honors the requested color and draws pure red markers and lines, matching matplotlib semantics.
Before (major): a single NaN in a continuous hue collapsed the entire color gradient, painting every point the same red.
After: the gradient survives a NaN hue value; points get their proper colors and the NaN point is shown neutrally in gray.
Before: the default hls palette is circular, so the minimum and maximum of a continuous hue (start and end of this spiral) were both red and visually indistinguishable.

After: the cyclic palette is trimmed so the endpoints differ -- the spiral now runs red-orange (hue=0) to magenta (hue=max), with a colorbar confirming a monotonic gradient. (Maintainer sign-off item.)
Before (major): at frame 10 the chemtrails animation had already drawn nearly the whole FUTURE trajectory as faint 'past' trails, leaking data the animation had not reached yet.
After: the same frame 10 shows only the trail actually traversed so far; the future trajectory stays hidden until the head reaches it.
Before (major): the plotly backend's surface= NaN'd out 299 of 300 data points enclosed by their own hulls -- opaque blobs with the scatter data silently deleted.
After: all 300 points are kept and the hulls are genuinely translucent (alpha=0.2 shown), so the enclosed scatter data is clearly visible through the surfaces.
After (was a crash, so no before image exists): hyp.plot on a plain Python list-of-lists numeric matrix, which previously died with an internal "color=" ValueError, now just plots.
Before (major): with a marker+line combo fmt on two datasets, markers took a different palette color than their own line -- every dataset showed cyan dots on red lines.
After: markers and lines are paired per dataset -- dataset 1 is fully red, dataset 2 fully cyan, so the two trajectories are actually distinguishable.
Before (major): combining animation with a continuous hue silently rendered a static plot -- at frame 10 the entire hue-colored trajectory was already fully drawn (no animation at all).
After: the same frame 10 shows a real animation window -- only the beginning of the hue-colored trajectory has been revealed so far.
Before: animating a surface dropped its per-vertex hue coloring -- the hull around a rainbow-colored helix rendered as a flat near-gray shell.
After: animated surface frames keep the per-vertex hue tint (pink/green/red regions match the local helix colors), identical to the static rendering.
